cards.front: Why can't a recurrent network process the positions of one training sentence in parallel?
cards.back: Each hidden state h_t is computed from the previous state h_(t-1) and the input at t, so positions must be computed in order. At long lengths, memory limits also cap batching across examples.

cards.front: Self-attention vs. a recurrent layer: how many sequential steps, and how long is the longest path between two positions?
cards.back: Self-attention: O(1) sequential operations and O(1) maximum path length. Recurrent: O(n) for both. Shorter paths make long-range dependencies easier to learn.

cards.front: Why are the dot products in attention divided by √d_k?
cards.back: For large d_k, dot products grow large (variance d_k if components have variance 1), which pushes softmax into regions with tiny gradients. The authors present this as a suspicion, not a proof.

cards.front: What happens if you replace 8 heads of size 64 with 1 head of size 512, keeping compute the same?
cards.back: Dev BLEU drops from 25.8 to 24.9. The paper's explanation: with one head, averaging stops the model from attending to different representation subspaces at once.

cards.front: What would go wrong if the decoder's self-attention were not masked?
cards.back: The prediction at position i could use outputs at positions i and later, breaking the auto-regressive property: each output must depend only on earlier outputs. Masking sets those softmax inputs to −∞.

cards.front: Encoder-decoder attention vs. encoder self-attention: where do the queries, keys, and values come from?
cards.back: Encoder-decoder: queries from the previous decoder layer; keys and values from the encoder output. Encoder self-attention: all three come from the previous encoder layer.

cards.front: Why does the Transformer need positional encodings when an RNN does not?
cards.back: With no recurrence and no convolution, nothing in the model carries word order. Positional encodings of size d_model are added to the input embeddings at the bottom of both stacks.

cards.front: Sinusoidal vs. learned positional encodings: how did they compare, and why did the authors keep sinusoids?
cards.back: Nearly identical results (dev BLEU 25.8 vs 25.7). Sinusoids were kept because they may extrapolate to longer sequences than seen in training, and because PE(pos+k) is a linear function of PE(pos). Neither reason is tested.

cards.front: When is a self-attention layer cheaper per layer than a recurrent layer?
cards.back: When sequence length n is smaller than representation size d: O(n²·d) vs O(n·d²). The authors say this usually holds for sentences split into word-pieces or byte-pairs.

cards.front: When would you restrict self-attention to a neighbourhood of size r, and what do you give up?
cards.back: For very long sequences. Per-layer cost falls to O(r·n·d), but the maximum path length rises from O(1) to O(n/r). The paper leaves this for future work.

cards.front: What happens to the base model if you turn dropout off (P_drop = 0)?
cards.back: Dev BLEU falls from 25.8 to 24.6 and perplexity rises from 4.92 to 5.77. The authors read this as dropout being very helpful against over-fitting.

cards.front: Label smoothing makes perplexity worse. Why use it anyway?
cards.back: It teaches the model to be less sure, which hurts perplexity but improves accuracy and BLEU. With ε_ls = 0 instead of 0.1, dev BLEU is 25.3 vs 25.8.

cards.front: ConvS2S, ByteNet, Transformer: how does the work to relate two distant positions grow with their distance?
cards.back: ConvS2S: linearly. ByteNet: logarithmically. Transformer: constant. The cost is lower effective resolution from averaging, which multi-head attention counteracts.

cards.front: What happens if you shrink the key size d_k from 64 to 16 and change nothing else?
cards.back: Dev BLEU drops from 25.8 to 25.1. The authors suggest computing compatibility is hard and a better function than the dot product may help. Parameters also drop (65M to 58M).

cards.front: Why do all sub-layers and embedding layers output vectors of the same size (512)?
cards.back: Each sub-layer is wrapped as LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)). Adding x to the sub-layer output only works if both have the same dimension, d_model = 512.

cards.front: Under the paper's learning-rate schedule, when does the rate go up and when does it go down?
cards.back: It rises linearly for the first warmup_steps = 4000 steps, then falls in proportion to 1/√(step number).

cards.front: Transformer big vs. base: what changes, and what does it buy on English-German?
cards.back: Big: d_model 1024, d_ff 4096, 16 heads, dropout 0.3, 300K steps, 213M parameters (base: 65M). Dev BLEU 26.4 vs 25.8; test BLEU 28.4 vs 27.3.
